text:
maria.thompson: quick heads-up — ran an overnight profiling sweep on model-x_small during the 11:30am spike. KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped from ~78% -> ~43% for 1-3 token prefixes, and we saw 6 OOM kills on the GPU pool. suspect warmup/backpressure + fragmentation. sharing notes + want recommendations on TTL shaping + batching heuristics.
ajay.patel: can you paste the profiler numbers/snippets? interested in hit-rate by prefix len and memory map.
maria.thompson: sure — pasted outputs below (abridged):
```
- total requests (window): 45k
- avg seq len: 96
- hit-rate overall: 62% -> midday dip to 43%
- hit-rate by prefix length: 1 tok: 29%, 2 tok: 35%, 3 tok: 42%, 4+ tok: 68%
- GPU mem free before OOM window: 4.8GB -> spikes down to 0.6GB
- fragmentation metric (slab): 18% -> 46% during spike
- evictions/sec: baseline 120 -> 820 at peak
```
kevin.li: interesting — low hit on short prefixes suggests key normalization or over-sharding of LRU. short prefixes tend to have high entropy; TTL might be too long for those so we keep lots of low-value entries.
sylvie: also note our LRU sharding is per-worker which causes shadowing when burst requests hit different shards. that increases effective footprint and fragmentation. switching to a smaller shard count (or global LRU) helped in previous runs.
ajay.patel: two quick angles: 1) TTL shaping by prefix-length / frequency (short prefixes get short TTLs), 2) warmup prefetch for long sessions so the KV cache warms before heavy generation. also consider moving tiny prefixes to a bloomcache with sampling — cheap check then skip heavy rejit.
maria.thompson: agree. any concrete formulas?
kevin.li: propose TTL = base_ttl * (1 + log(1 + freq_rank)) * length_factor, where length_factor = clamp(seq_len/16, 0.25, 2.0). Practically: 1-2 token prefixes -> ttl = 30s, 3-5 -> 2m, 6+ -> 10m. That should reduce churn from noisy short keys.
sylvie: on eviction: we should measure live fragmentation and run a compaction job during low-traffic windows. also tweak slab sizing to reduce small-allocation waste. we can add a fragmentation alert (ops-bot) when slab_frag > 30% for >5min.
kevin.li: batching heuristic: current static target batch size 32. When we see many short prefixes and low cache hits, small-request-first ordering helps reuse KV cache across the batch: sort by prefix-length ascending before batching. Also make batch_adaptive: if avg_hit_rate < 50% reduce max_batch_size to 8 to lower memory footprint and avoid large KV cache per-batch allocations.
ajay.patel: +1. Also add an admission policy: if request appears cold (no recent hits), mark it as low-priority and schedule for background warmup (best-effort) instead of blocking foreground kernel allocation. That buys time for cache warming.
ops-bot: Alert: gpu-pool-7 OOM_KILL count increased by 6 in the last 15m. Current slab_frag: 46%. Eviction rate: 820/s.
maria.thompson: posting a quick config mock-up for TTL / batching (proof-of-concept):
```
{
  "kv_cache": {
    "ttl_policy": [
      {"prefix_len_max": 2, "ttl_s": 30},
      {"prefix_len_max": 5, "ttl_s": 120},
      {"prefix_len_max": 999, "ttl_s": 600}
    ],
    "hotset_threshold": 0.02,
    "shard_count": 8
  },
  "batching": {
    "mode": "adaptive",
    "target_batch": 32,
    "min_batch": 4,
    "reduce_on_low_hit": {"threshold": 0.5, "new_target": 8},
    "ordering": "prefix_len_asc"
  }
}
```
sylvie: can we also flip a kernel fallback to a lower memory quantized kernel when free_mem < 1GB? kernel_switch is cheap vs OOM. we need a fast path to swap kernel variants on the fly.
kevin.li: yes — runtime already has selective kernel selection. add a policy: if gpu_free < 1GB OR slab_frag > 35% OR eviction_rate > 500/s then prefer q8_fallback kernel. fallback should be per-model-instance, not global to avoid perf cliffs for unrelated models.
ajay.patel: we should run two small experiments: A) TTL-shape (per-prefix TTL) vs global TTL, and B) adaptive batching + prefix ordering vs baseline. measure: 1) end-to-end p95 latency, 2) cache hit-rate by prefix len, 3) GPU OOM/kills, 4) tokens per second / $cost. run both as canary on 10% traffic for 48h.
maria.thompson: sounds good. my proposed owners and tasks:
- maria: implement TTL policy + fragmentation alert (PR + canary)
- kevin: batching adaptivity + ordering patch
- sylvie: slab sizing + kernel-fallback policy + compaction job
- ajay: experiment harness + metrics dashboards (per-prefix hit-rate)
- ops-bot: will gatecanary and surface alerts

maria.thompson: timeline? aim to land TTL/alert + dashboard today, start canary tomorrow morning. any blockers? :thumbsup:
kevin.li: no blockers from my side, will open PR for batching tonight.
ajay.patel: will scaffold dashboards and experiment configs.
sylvie: need a quick approval for a low-risk compaction script — posting patch shortly.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: eng-runtime/canary-ttl-batch at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z for 48h (10% traffic).
maria.thompson: thanks all — will follow up with perf numbers once canary starts. keep reactions in thread.
